last.verdict: Cloud growth sped up and spending came in lower than feared, so shares rose.

reasons.label: Azure growth accelerated
reasons.text: Azure revenue grew 48%, above the 44%–45% range Microsoft had guided.

reasons.label: Lower AI spending
reasons.text: Capex was about $39.4B, below the $45.9B analysts expected; lease accounting may flatter it.

reasons.label: Beat on revenue, profit
reasons.text: Revenue of $92.3B and adjusted EPS of $4.89 topped forecasts of $90.6B and $4.73.

story: Microsoft fell about 10% in January on heavy AI spending and OpenAI exposure, slipped again in April despite Azure growth near 40%, then jumped about 9% in July. Azure has since sped up to 48%, and investors keep watching spending.
